//: Story Phase 2, chapter 5: The Cloud Takes the Ship. The crew has evacuated to the main deck (CLOUD placements in main_deck.patch.json); Garrick stands at (7,21), Squawks at (9,18).

ch5.begin.tutorial: Thick yellow fumes fill your Exposure meter. Get out of them before it fills, or you'll collapse. A light haze is harmless, and you recover in clean air.
ch5.begin.title: Fumes

ch5.deck_arrival: The whole crew is on deck: coughing, hanging over the rails, fanning each other with hats.
hale[coughing]: Captain! Thank the tides. Everyone's out. Everyone we can count.
quill[coughing]: I've counted twice, Captain. The count keeps coming out 'yellow'.
mags[disgusted]: My galley. My beautiful galley.
jim[angry]: I TOLD you, Captain. Didn't I tell you?
brask[coughing]: My eyes are watering and I'm not even sad.
wick[alarmed]: Is this what the end of the world smells like?
finch: Forty years at sea. Never smelled the like. Not even the time with the dead whale.
bob[happy]: ...Tastes a bit like spicy sunshine.
ned[alarmed]: Captain. Captain, look at the figurehead.
For sixty years the figurehead of the Queen Anne's Revenge has gazed out to sea with serene oak dignity.
She has never once changed her expression.
garrick[nervous]: Captain. Before you say anything—
hale[coughing]: Captain, what IS this? Will it pass?

start: garrick[businesslike]: Right. Everyone, gather round. Not too close. Upwind, ideally.
garrick: What you're experiencing is what we in the trade call a Gust. It happens to me every few years. Usually I'm alone. Usually I'm outdoors.
captain: And this time?
garrick: This time I was in a sealed room full of metal, after a lunch of—
jim[angry]: TWELVE. ONIONS.
garrick[pretend]: —a varied lunch.
garrick[worried]: Now. Every Gust has a Dead Center. The place it started. The air there isn't air any more. It's more of a... soup.
garrick: The cloud settles. It sinks to the lowest point it can find and it sits there, thick as porridge. Here on deck? Unpleasant.
garrick[nervous]: Down there, in the Dead Center... I wouldn't stay long. Nobody should stay long.
fennimore[concerned]: Are you telling us it could kill a man?
garrick[nervous]: I'm telling you it's never been tested. Nobody's ever been willing.
captain[angry]: What was IN that lunch, Guzzlegut?
garrick: The usual. And the sausages.
captain: The sausages you paddled here with.
garrick[pretend]: Ah. About those. They weren't sausages, strictly. Well, they were sausages. They were bait sausages.
jim[alarmed]: BAIT?!
garrick[businesslike]: Crab bait. Premium grade, three weeks old, extremely potent. Crabs go wild for it.
captain[disgusted]: ...There was a crab on my door.
garrick[smug]: Loyal customers.
jim[angry]: And the eel paste! The jar SAID do not open below deck!
garrick[businesslike]: It said not to open it below deck. That's where the jar was.
jim[surprised]: That's— that isn't— you can't—
captain[resigned]: Don't, Jim. Don't argue with him. It only encourages him.
fall: squawks[furious]: SQUAWK! YOU! BATHTUB MAN! You've ruined the treasure, you've ruined the galley, you've ruined the AIR—
A gust of honest sea wind snaps the mainsail full—
nell[alarmed]: He went down the hatch! Straight into it!
garrick[terrified]: Down there? Captain, the cloud's pooling at the lowest point of the ship. The hold. By the treasure door.
captain[determined]: Then that's where I'm going.
